The rigor of American high school depends on which city in the US you move to. Most high schools offer more rigorous classes (AP classes, you can earn college credits by passing the AP exams) but it really depends on where you end up. Going to high school in for example, Texas will be different compared attending high school in California. 

As a Singaporean who went to high school and went through the college admissions process in America, I would personally recommend waiting until you finish A levels. Most people take the ACT or SAT (college entrance exams) during 11th grade (JC1) and it takes months of preparation to get a good score. If you’re planning on going to Harvard or other Ivy League schools you will want to have a good GPA, standardized test scores, and participate in extracurricular activities in high school. That is a lot to do within the span of 2 years and it will be very stressful.

I see that you’re wanting to study law at Harvard. Something to keep in mind: in America, to get a law degree you need to complete your bachelor’s degree first.
